$comment: The conformance suites, declared once. `generate_ci.py` emits the oracle jobs of
.github/workflows/ci.yml from this file, and `run_suite.py` runs the same steps locally.
`status` is `oracle-backed` (CI regenerates the golden in the pinned container and compares
it on every run) or `unchecked` (the golden is committed and read by the Rust tests, but no
CI step has ever re-derived it). The distinction is part of the claim each suite supports.
Jobs that are analysis rather than comparison stay hand-written in ci.template.yml: the
jmath corpus diff and the pow probe of decision 0007, and the JVM number-format sweep of
decision 0017, which asserts measured rates rather than byte equality.

ci.$why: Suites are grouped into jobs of this size: one job per suite would restore the oracle image once per suite, and one job for all of them is what the hand-written workflow did, where a failing suite hid every suite after it.

suites.title: The BED codec
suites.why: BEDCodec is what GATK's -L regions.bed runs through, so its coordinate convention is the one a whole interval argument inherits, and five of its decisions are not what a BED parser suggests. The start is shifted by a constructor argument, StartOffset.ONE being the default, so a file's 0-based start becomes 1-based on the way in and the feature carries the shifted number without carrying the shift. A two-token line is a point rather than a zero-length interval, because with no end column the end is the shifted start: one base at a coordinate the file never mentions. The separator is the regex tab-or-a-run-of-spaces with limit -1, so a run of spaces however long is one separator, a tab beside a space is two, and a trailing separator produces an empty field rather than being dropped. A blank line and a header line decode to null rather than to an error, and the header prefixes are matched on the raw line so a leading space makes them data. And a score that does not parse returns the feature early, so a line whose score is a dot keeps its name and silently loses its strand, its colour and its exons even though those columns are present and well formed, while every other malformed number in the same line throws instead.

suites.title: The IntervalList codec
suites.why: IntervalListCodec is what GATK's -L regions.interval_list runs through, and it is a stricter parser than the reader htsjdk uses on the same file, so whether an interval list is valid depends on which door it came through. The field count is checked against five exactly and is counted after String.split has dropped trailing empty fields, so a line ending in a tab is refused for its count rather than for its empty name. The strand column is decoded by Strand.decode, which answers NONE for anything that is not a single plus or minus, and NONE is then rejected, so a dot is a legal strand in the BED codec of the same package and an error here. An interval on a contig the dictionary does not hold is dropped with a warning and the file still loads, while an interval past the end of a contig it does hold fails the whole read, and that length check is switched off by a declared length of zero. And start equal to end plus one is a legal empty interval while start equal to end plus two is refused with a message quoting a film, which is observable output and therefore part of the port.

suites.title: VCFCodec.canDecode, the codec that opens the file
suites.why: VCFCodec is the third codec GATK's -L reaches and the only one that decides by content rather than by path. BEDCodec and IntervalListCodec answer canDecode on the extension, so a .list holding a BED body is not a Feature file and dies in the interval reader; a .list holding a VCF body is one, because this codec reads the first eighteen bytes and finds the magic. Two files with the same extension and different contents therefore take different branches of -L, and only this codec makes that true. It tries plain, then GZIPInputStream, then BlockCompressedInputStream, and since a BGZF file is a gzip file the second attempt already answers for the third. The read's return value is computed and never used, so a file shorter than the magic leaves zero bytes in the tail of the buffer and answers false rather than throwing, and an absent path answers false through a caught IOException. The magic carries no minor version, so 4.0 through 4.3 all match and 3.3 does not; VCF3Codec carries the other magic and GATK registers both.

suites.why: The BAM record codec is pure integer work, so unlike the math corpus there is no reason to expect emulation to change it. That is the hypothesis; this measures it, because "no reason to expect" is how decision 0004's wrong assumption got in.

suites.title: Which @HD version a written BAM carries
suites.why: BAMFileWriter has two header paths and they disagree. The ordinary writer goes through SAMFileWriterImpl.writeHeader, which encodes with keepExistingVersionNumber = FALSE and rebuilds the @HD line from a fresh SAMFileHeader, so a written BAM carries the CURRENT version whatever the input said. The static BAMFileWriter.writeHeader(BinaryCodec, SAMFileHeader) passes TRUE and keeps it, and is only reachable from the block-copy reheader path. This port calls one function for both and keeps the input's version in each, which is right for the reheader and wrong for the writer. No existing fixture can see it: every one of them builds its header with new SAMFileHeader(), whose constructor already sets the current version. The dump also asks whether VN can sit anywhere but first, since the reference rebuilds the line rather than editing it, and records the answer rather than assuming it.

cases.why: 8 rows, no files: four headers, each encoded with keepExistingVersionNumber = true and also written through SAMFileWriterFactory. One already current, one at VN:1.5, one at VN:1.5 parsed from text whose @HD line puts SO before VN, and one at VN:1.4 beside a sort order. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32197064547, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: The FASTA, the .fai and the .dict FastaReferenceWriter writes
suites.why: Three GATK tools write a reference through this class and none of them can be ported until it is. THE INDEX OFFSET IS TAKEN AFTER THE HEADER LINE, so it counts this sequence's header bytes and every byte before it. BYTES-PER-LINE IS BASES-PER-LINE PLUS ONE always, even for a sequence shorter than one line. A SEQUENCE IS TERMINATED BY EXACTLY ONE NEWLINE, written when the sequence is closed rather than after each line, so a length that is a multiple of the width gets no blank line. THE LINE WIDTH IS PER SEQUENCE rather than per file. APPENDING IN CHUNKS IS THE SAME FILE as appending at once, because the breaks come from a running count. THE MD5 IS OF THE UPPER-CASED BASES, computed chunk by chunk, so a lower-case sequence keeps its case in the FASTA and hashes as though it did not. AND THE REFUSALS ARE PART OF THE CONTRACT: a blank in a name, a control character, an empty name, a sequence with no bases, a repeated name, a base that is not IUPAC and a line width of zero are each a different class or message, while a TAB in a description is allowed.

cases.why: 38 rows, no files: eight writers run to completion and eleven run into a refusal, each printing its FASTA, its .fai and its .dict as escaped text. The eight cover the default width, a width that divides the length, a sequence shorter than one line, two sequences at different widths in one file, the same sequence appended in three unaligned chunks, mixed case with IUPAC codes, and the md5 over lower and upper case. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32272833549, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.why: The reheadered BAM is block-copied, so it carries compressed bytes and depends on the deflate pin (decision 0001), exactly like the BAM file goldens. Comment rows share a (kind, case) key so only the last per case is diffed here, but the reheadered hex encodes every comment in its header, so any comment drift shows up there.

suites.title: BAM gather

suites.title: Reading a tag block, and the two types that do not survive a round trip
suites.why: The write side of BinaryTagCodec is pinned; this is the read side, which is what the CRAM slice header's tag section and every BAM record's tags come back through. EVERY NARROW INTEGER WIDENS TO ONE TYPE: c, C, s, S and i all return a Java Integer, so the width the file chose stops existing on the way in and the type a rewrite picks comes from the value alone. THE ROUND TRIP IS NOT THE IDENTITY, AND EXACTLY TWO TYPES BREAK IT: an 'I' holding a small value is rewritten as 'c', and an 'H' is rewritten as a 'B' array one byte longer. THERE IS NO IN-MEMORY H AT ALL: it decodes into the same byte[] a signed B array does, so both codecs carry a dead branch for writing one back, and XX:H:48656C re-encodes as XX:B:c,72,101,108. 'A' IS A SIGNED BYTE CAST TO A CHAR, so the byte 0xE9 becomes U+FFE9 and the character in memory is not the one in the file, though the bytes survive because the write truncates it back. THE 'I' RANGE CHECK CANNOT FIRE, because the value is masked to 32 bits before it is checked against the 32-bit range. THE LIST COMES BACK SORTED BY THE PACKED SHORT, so by the SECOND character first, and a repeated tag replaces rather than duplicates, with the LAST occurrence winning. AND THE UNSIGNED FLAG OF AN ARRAY IS ONLY THE CASE OF ITS TYPE LETTER: the elements stay signed, so a C array holding 0xFF comes back as -1.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the candidate-goldens-bam-tag-read artefact of run 31093032906, the golden-pending run of htsjdk-rs #123. 62 rows built from bytes the dump lays out itself rather than from a file htsjdk wrote, because the two most interesting inputs are ones htsjdk never writes: an 'I' holding a small value and an 'H' at all. Every row carries the bytes it came from, so the golden is readable without the dump beside it. The runner's dump and this laptop's are byte-identical, which is recorded and changes nothing: decision 0008 says where a golden may come from, not how likely the two are to agree.

suites.title: VCF headers
Reading a VCF header
suites.why: Everything else here writes VCF; nothing reads one, and GATK's VariantWalker cannot exist without a reader. Two layers are measured. VCFHeaderLineTranslator's VCF4Parser is a hand-written scanner whose switch falls through from the '<' case into the '>' case, so an unquoted '<' away from position 0 is dropped, an unquoted '>' anywhere is dropped, and a line that does not end in '>' loses its last field entirely and silently: a port written from the VCF specification would keep those characters and store that field. Quotes are a toggle rather than a delimiter, because the quote test precedes the in-quote test, so a quote in the middle of an unquoted value opens a quoted region and the comma after it stops separating fields; inside a quote a backslash before anything but a quote or a backslash is kept together with the character. VCFCodec.readActualHeader is the second layer: it splits the version line on every '=' and records a version only when that yields exactly two fields, so a line with an extra '=' records nothing and fails later with a different message. The refusals carry their messages because the messages separate two failures of the same file. Only unstructured meta lines are fed to the frame; turning an INFO line into a typed compound header line is the next layer and is measured on its own, since mixing them would leave a failure ambiguous between the two.

suites.title: One ## line into a typed header line
suites.why: The scanner suite says which pairs a line carries; this says what they mean, and it is where the refusals are. Four different exception classes come out of this layer and which one a file gets is a property of the field that is wrong: Number=x throws java.lang.NumberFormatException because nothing wraps Integer.parseInt, Number=-1 throws TribbleException$InvalidHeader, Number=0 on a non-Flag type throws java.lang.IllegalArgumentException from validate(), and Type=integer throws a plain TribbleException without the malformed-header prefix. Two of those are unchecked Java exceptions that no catch in the codec touches, so a malformed Number does not report a malformed header at all, and a port that funnelled every failure into one error type would answer a different question. Three asymmetries make the same line valid or invalid depending on context rather than on the line: INFO allows Type=Flag and FORMAT does not; a Flag with a non-zero count is silently rewritten to zero rather than refused, which is a value change and not an error; and Source and Version are read only from VCF 4.2, while under 4.1 they are not recommended tags either, so the tag-order check rejects the same line the 4.2 codec accepts. The rendered line is compared rather than the fields, because the rendering is what a writer emits and it carries the quoting rule as well as the values.

suites.title: VCF records
Whole VCF files
Reading one VCF data line
suites.why: The vcf-record suite measures writing a record; this measures reading one, which is what GATK's VariantWalker needs and what nothing here has done before. Genotypes are excluded on purpose: htsjdk defers them through LazyGenotypesContext and the deferral is itself observable, so it is its own slice, and this stops at the eight site columns. Five behaviours decide what a record means and none is in the VCF specification. The splitter is not String.split: ParsingUtils.split fills a fixed-size array, steps over a delimiter at position zero instead of producing an empty first token, and condenses every trailing column into the last slot, so a line starting with a tab loses its first character and every genotype column after the first arrives joined back together in parts[8], which is why the column check compares against nine whatever the sample count. END overrides the stop and nothing validates it, so a record can end before it starts. A declared Flag written as KEY=0 is dropped from the attributes entirely rather than stored as false, and a bare key whose header type is not Flag becomes the string "." rather than a flag, so the header changes what a record contains. REF is upper-cased silently, so a lower-case REF is a rewrite and not an error. And an ALT of "." is checked and then not added, so the record carries one allele rather than two. The refusals are compared with their classes because parseQual throws a NumberFormatException that nothing catches while the neighbouring failures are TribbleExceptions carrying a line number. Attributes and filters are sorted in the dump: they live in a HashMap and a HashSet upstream, so their iteration order is not a property of the file and comparing it would compare the JDK.

suites.title: Reading the genotype columns
suites.why: The vcf-record-parse suite stops at the eight site columns; this is the rest, which htsjdk defers through LazyGenotypesContext until something asks for it. Four behaviours decide what a genotype contains and none is in the VCF specification. The GT separators are three characters, not two: VCFConstants.PHASING_TOKENS is a slash, a pipe and a backslash, and the split is a StringTokenizer, which drops empty tokens, so a backslash separates alleles like a slash does and 0//1, /0/1 and 0/1/ all yield the same two alleles as 0/1. A malformed AD or PL is silently dropped, because decodeInts catches NumberFormatException and returns null, which the builder stores as no-AD, while two lines further down the same method DP goes through a bare Integer.parseInt whose failure is not caught at all: the same malformed integer either disappears or aborts the record, decided by which key it was under. GT must be at position 0 when present and, before VCF 4.1, must be present at all, so the same record is valid or invalid depending on a header line. And a key with no value is skipped just as a value of "." is, but only the second had to be looked at, which shows in FT where "." means unfiltered rather than absent. GL is excluded: converting it to PL runs through GenotypeLikelihoods.fromGLField, which is floating-point work with its own rounding, and folding it in here would mix a numeric question into a parsing one.

suites.title: Reading a whole VCF file
suites.why: H.2's read side above the line: the loop that joins the header frame, one data line and one genotype block, each of which already has a suite, into a whole file. The state the codec carries BETWEEN those calls is what this measures, and none of it is visible in a single line. The line counter is shared and incremented in two places, so the SAME malformed line reports two different numbers: decodeLine's column check runs before parseVCFLine's lineNo++ and generateException runs after it, measured here as Line 12 and line number 13 for two records at the same file line. A line beginning with '#' anywhere in the body decodes to null rather than to a record or a refusal, so a reader that collects decode results silently loses records. The version is read once and it selects a text transformer applied to every INFO and every genotype value for the rest of the file, so the same data line means different things in a v4.2 file and a v4.3 one; the decode also runs BEFORE the Flag test, so under 4.3 a declared Flag written DB=%30 is dropped exactly as DB=0 is. That transformer's decoder is Integer.parseInt(s, 16), which accepts a sign, so %+1 is U+0001 and %-1 is left alone, and a failed escape is emitted with the '%' NOT skipped, which is why %%41 decodes to %A. And the header handed back is not the header the file contains: doOnTheFlyModifications defaults to true, so a standard INFO or FORMAT ID whose count or type disagrees with htsjdk's is replaced WHOLESALE, description included, while a description that disagrees on its own is kept because REPAIR_BAD_DESCRIPTIONS is false; and the file's own fileformat line is deleted by the VCFHeader constructor and a SYNTHESIZED one prepended by getMetaDataInInputOrder, which says VCFv4.2 for everything below 4.3, so a v4.0 file reads back claiming to be v4.2. The repair also rebuilds the header through a constructor that takes no version and re-attaches it only from 4.3, so below 4.3 the codec knows the version and the header does not. The round trip is measured rather than assumed: reading a file and writing it back is not the identity, and a v4.3 file cannot be written back at all.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the candidate-goldens artefact of the golden-pending run of htsjdk-rs #98. 102 rows: 24 whole-file reads, 13 headers as the codec hands them back, 20 percent-decoder cases and 3 round trips. The rows that carry the suite are the two line numbers for the same position, the fileformat line the reader substitutes for the file's, and the standard header lines it rewrites.

suites.title: A VCF and its .idx written in one pass
suites.why: The join between the VCF the writer emits and the .idx it writes beside it, which is what every GATK tool emitting a VCF does and what neither the vcf-file suite nor tribble-index-write can see alone. INDEX_ON_THE_FLY IS ON BY DEFAULT: VariantContextWriterBuilder.DEFAULT_OPTIONS is EnumSet.of(Options.INDEX_ON_THE_FLY), so a caller who asks for nothing gets an index, and one who asks for nothing AND supplies no dictionary gets an exception instead of a file. THE RECORDED POSITION IS THE ONE BEFORE THE RECORD, and it is absolute in the output stream, so THE HEADER IS COUNTED: measured, the first record sits at 242 because that is the header's length, and an index built from a feature list that forgot the header is uniformly off by it. THE SEQUENCE DICTIONARY BECOMES PROPERTIES, NOT A FLAG: setIndexSequenceDictionary writes one DICT:<contig> property per sequence and flags stays ZERO, because SEQUENCE_DICTIONARY_FLAG is only read for version < 3; and those properties come BEFORE the dynamic creator's four statistics, because finalizeIndex copies the creator's own map first. AND THE LAYOUT IS NOT THE CALLER'S CHOICE: the writer always uses a DynamicIndexCreator with FOR_SEEK_TIME, so measured on ordinary files, one record gets a linear index while two thousand records get an interval tree, as does a header-only file, whose feature density is a division of zero by zero. Two refusals are measured and one is not the documented one: indexing to a stream is documented as an IllegalArgumentException and arrives as a NullPointerException, after the VCF itself has already been written.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the candidate-goldens artefact of the golden-pending run of htsjdk-rs #101. 26 rows: 7 written VCFs with every record's byte offset, 7 index files, 6 property sets, 4 per-contig records and 2 refusals. Six index files are compared BYTE FOR BYTE across both layouts, three of them interval trees, with the header's path, size, timestamp and MD5 taken from the golden because they are facts about the run rather than decisions of the writer. The VCF rows compare the file's length, the header's length and every record's offset, which is what pins the two halves to each other: an index whose positions are right about a file the port writes differently is wrong twice and passes neither row.

suites.title: GL to PL, and the double parser under it
suites.why: A genotype carrying GL and no PL gets its PL computed here and every downstream tool reads the PL, so this is the last thing between a VCF with likelihoods in it and a port that can decode it. Three layers, and each has a decision a port gets wrong by default. Double.parseDouble is not Rust's f64 parser: Java accepts a trailing type suffix, hexadecimal floating point with a mandatory p exponent, leading and trailing whitespace up to and including the space character, and the spelled-out Infinity, while Rust accepts none of those and accepts inf and nan, which Java does not. VCFUtils.parseVcfDouble then catches the failure and retries against a case-insensitive infinity-or-NaN pattern, so inf and -INFINITY and nan parse after all, but only after the plain parse has failed. And GLsToPLs is one line with three decisions: the adjustment is the maximum of the likelihoods so the conversion re-normalises and the best genotype always comes out at zero whatever the input scale; MAX_PL is Integer.MAX_VALUE and the clamp is applied to the double before the rounding; and Math.round is floor of x plus a half, so it rounds half up rather than half away from zero, answers zero for a NaN, and returns a long that is then truncated to int. Reordering any of the three agrees on every ordinary genotype. The parsed doubles travel as raw bits, because a decimal rendering of a parse result hides exactly the disagreements this suite exists to find.

suites.title: AC, AF and AN
suites.why: GATK's ChromosomeCounts annotation is two lines that delegate straight to VariantContextUtils.calculateChromosomeCounts, so this is where the three commonest INFO fields in any VCF are decided, and four of its behaviours do not follow from the field names. AC and AF change type with the number of alternate alleles, one alt giving a scalar and two or more a list, so a consumer that fetched AC gets an Integer in one case and an ArrayList in the other even though both render the same way. A genotype whose FT is set contributes nothing and so does a no-call allele, for different reasons, which means AN is not the ploidy times the sample count. AF is not AC over AN: the numerator is the founders count for that allele and the denominator the founders total called count, while the AC reported alongside is the whole cohort's, so a port computing AF from the AC it has just written agrees on every unrelated cohort and disagrees on every pedigree. And the function removes keys as well as adding them, deleting AC and AF at a site with no alternate allele and all three where nobody is called, but only when removeStaleValues is on, which the annotation hard-codes to true. AF travels as raw bits because it is a division and a decimal rendering would hide a divergence in the last place.

suites.title: The genotype type ladder
suites.why: Genotype.determineType decides what every consumer downstream means by het and by called, and three of its answers contradict the javadoc above them. HET is two called alleles that are not equal, so C/G with no reference allele in it is HET, which is why isHetNonRef exists as a separate question and why a port defining HET as one ref and one alt disagrees on every multiallelic site. Equality is Allele.equals, which is bases and the reference flag, so a genotype holding the reference A and a non-reference A is HET while printing as A/A. And ploidy is not two: a haploid call is HOM_REF or HOM_VAR and never HET, a triploid A/A/C is HET, and MIXED is any genotype with at least one call and one no-call whatever its ploidy. VariantContext.isMonomorphicInSamples is measured alongside because it is the guard on GATK's SampleList annotation and it is not every genotype is hom-ref: a site carrying alternate alleles and no genotypes is not monomorphic, since the first disjunct needs no alternate allele and the second needs genotypes. The name order is measured because getGenotypesOrderedByName sorts with Collections.sort, which is String.compareTo, which is UTF-16 code units: uppercase before lowercase, 10 before 2, and a supplementary character BELOW U+FFFF because the first unit of its surrogate pair is 0xD83D, which is the opposite of code-point order and therefore the opposite of what Rust str comparison gives.

suites.title: What a declared Type actually does
suites.why: H.2's last open item, full field-type coverage, and the measurement is that the declared Type converts NOTHING. Every Type in the format stores a String, or a list of Strings when Number is not 1, with the single exception of Flag, which stores a boolean: Integer, Float, Character and String are indistinguishable in a decoded record. The header's Type only tells a caller which accessor to reach for, and the conversion happens there, once per call, with a default the caller supplies. THE MISSING TEST IS A REFERENCE COMPARISON: getAttributeAsInt reads x == VCFConstants.MISSING_VALUE_v4, with ==, on a String, true only when the stored object IS that constant. The codec assigns the constant for a bare key and for KEY=, so those return the default; a value written KEY=. arrives as a substring of the line and reaches Integer.parseInt(".") instead. Three spellings of missing, identical in every rendering, two outcomes, and the two are a number and an exception. getAttributeAsDouble DOES NOT HAVE THE TEST AT ALL, so all three spellings throw there, while getAttributeAsDoubleList DOES have it: two accessors over the same conversion that disagree about what missing means. A scalar accessor reaching a list or a flag fails the CAST and not the parse, and the message names the stored class, so a list and a flag produce two different exceptions. And parseVcfDouble is not Double.parseDouble: on failure it retries against an infinity-or-NaN pattern, while Double.parseDouble itself already accepts surrounding whitespace, a trailing f or d, and hex float literals, so 1f, 1d, 0x1p3 and " 1" are all numbers to a VCF reader.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the candidate-goldens artefact of the golden-pending run of htsjdk-rs #102. 253 rows: 25 stored values with the Java class each reports, 200 accessor results across eight accessors, and 28 parseVcfDouble inputs. The rows that carry the suite are the three spellings of missing, which render identically and answer differently, and the class name inside each ClassCastException, which names the STORED class and so differs between a list and a flag reaching the same accessor.

CigarUtil soft clip

suites.title: Percentile, Median and FastMath.round
suites.why: MathUtils.median in GATK goes through commons-math3 Percentile, which is Apache 2.0 and therefore transcribable where the JDK's own math is not (decision 0023). Four things here are not what the median suggests. The estimator interpolates, and its arithmetic is lower + dif * (upper - lower) rather than the mean of the two central values, which is a different double when they are far apart. The default NaN strategy is REMOVED, so a NaN shortens the array instead of ranking to an end, and an array of nothing but NaN answers NaN by way of an empty array. A single value is returned before the NaN strategy runs at all, so one NaN and two NaNs reach the same answer down different paths. And MathUtils.median finishes with FastMath.round, which is (long) floor(x + 0.5): the definition java.lang.Math.round stopped using in Java 7, so the two are one apart on 0.49999999999999994 and a port that reused the Math.round already in this crate would be wrong there. The jar is pinned to 3.5 because GATK's build.gradle declares strictly 3.5; the jmath corpus job downloads 3.6.1 for its FastMath columns, and that disagreement between two pins in this repository is open. Sixteen of its 312 percentile rows are an invalid operation's NaN, produced by the interpolation over infinities; x86-64 sets the sign bit and AArch64 does not, so the test exempts a NaN-sign-only difference off x86-64 and counts it, and asserts zero exemptions on the oracle's own architecture. That is decision 0012 reached by a second route.

suites.title: FastMath.exp, FastMath.log and their tables
suites.why: FastMath.exp is not java.lang.Math.exp. It is table-driven, pure Java and Apache 2.0, so unlike the HotSpot intrinsic withdrawn in decision 0014 it can be ported, and everything in commons-math3 that needs an exponential goes through it: Gamma, Erf, NormalDistribution, and therefore GATK's MannWhitneyU and every rank-sum annotation. The reference ships 6,175 lines of literal doubles for the four exponential tables and can also regenerate them with FastMathCalc, the choice being a compile-time constant set to the literals; the port was written on the computing branch and the oracle was asked whether the two branches agree. They do not: 577 of the 5,050 entries differ, all of them in the integer table, which is the only one built through splitReciprocal. That is decision 0024, and it means the port must carry the literals, since the literals are the branch that runs upstream. The golden carries both columns, read out of the same JVM, so the disagreement stays measured; 160 of the recomputed entries are an invalid operation's NaN, whose sign is the FPU's, which is decision 0012 arriving by a third route. The function itself is measured on the boundaries its own branches name: below -746 it underflows to zero, below -709 and at -709 it recurses on a shifted argument and divides by a magic constant so a subnormal result keeps its precision, and above 709 it overflows. The logarithm is here for the same reason and with the same two columns: eleven of the call sites in Gamma, Erf and NormalDistribution reach FastMath.log rather than Math.log, and the two differ in the last bit because only the JDK one is correctly rounded. Its table, LN_MANT, does agree with its recomputation, which places the disagreement of decision 0024 specifically on the reciprocal path rather than on FastMathCalc in general.

compare.why: The 160 entries of the two RECOMPUTED tables that come out NaN carry whichever sign produced them, and that is not reproducible. `inf / inf` gives x86's negative default quiet NaN when the FPU computes it and Java's positive canonical NaN when the JIT folds it, on the same architecture and in the same container: one CI runner produced each, and the second one failed against a golden the first had written. The golden is not regenerated, because it is a faithful record of what the oracle held; the comparison stops asserting a bit no port could reproduce. Only NaN patterns are collapsed, so every finite value still travels bit for bit.

suites.title: Gamma, Erf and the normal distribution
suites.why: Erf is the whole of NormalDistribution.cumulativeProbability, which is the whole of the normal approximation in GATK's MannWhitneyU, which is what every rank-sum annotation reports, so these three files decide the last digit of MQRankSum. Four of their decisions are not what the names suggest. erf is not a polynomial approximation but an incomplete gamma function evaluated by series or continued fraction, stopped by a relative tolerance of 1e-15 or by ten thousand iterations, so where the iteration stops is part of the result. regularizedGammaP delegates to regularizedGammaQ when x is at least a plus one and Q delegates back to P below that, so the pair is one function with a switch in the middle and the two sides are computed by different algorithms. erf and erfInv are inverses in mathematics and unrelated in code, one being a gamma integral and the other a rational approximation, so a round trip does not return its input, and MannWhitneyU makes exactly that round trip. And both erf and cumulativeProbability shortcut beyond forty, returning exactly zero, one or minus one without computing anything, so each is discontinuous at a value the author chose.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner. 1,226 answers, 34 of them refusals, and the golden corrected the port on one: inverseCumulativeProbability guards with p < 0 || p > 1, both of which are false for NaN, so a NaN probability is not out of range to the reference and flows through to come back as NaN. The port had used a range check, which refuses it. Three rows are an invalid operation's NaN whose sign is the FPU's, exempted off x86-64 and counted, which is decision 0012.

suites.title: The saddle-point expansion and the hypergeometric log probability
suites.why: GATK's FisherExactTest builds a HypergeometricDistribution and asks it for the log probability of every point of the support, so this is the arithmetic under FS, the Fisher-strand annotation. getStirlingError has three algorithms: below fifteen and on a half-integer it reads a table of literals, below fifteen and off a half-integer it goes through logGamma, and at fifteen and above it is a five-term asymptotic series, with the boundaries as exact comparisons on a double. The table's last entry is dead code, because the guard is z below fifteen and fifteen itself takes the series; the two disagree in the thirteenth digit, which is the size of the discontinuity the table exists to avoid. getDeviancePart iterates until an addition stops moving the double, so it terminates on the rounding rather than on a tolerance. And logBinomialProbability has four branches at the ends of its range, chosen by comparing p or q against a tenth, of which only the middle one uses the Stirling error.

suites.title: The binomial quantile a noise floor is read off
suites.why: BinomialDistribution.inverseCumulativeProbability, which GATK reaches through PowerCalculationUtils.calculateMinCountForSignal. It is not a formula but a bracket narrowed by a one-sided Chebyshev inequality and then bisected, so where the bracket starts is part of the answer. THE ANSWER IS THE SMALLEST x WITH cdf(x) >= p and the bisection returns upper rather than lower. THE LOWER BOUND IS DECREMENTED BEFORE THE SEARCH, which is what makes the invariant true at the start. THE CHEBYSHEV NARROWING USES ceil AND THEN SUBTRACTS ONE on both ends, so the bracket is asymmetric. IT IS SKIPPED ENTIRELY when the variance is zero, which for a binomial means a probability of exactly zero or one. p = 0 RETURNS THE SUPPORT'S LOWER BOUND AND p = 1 ITS UPPER, before any search. AND A p OUTSIDE THE UNIT INTERVAL IS AN OutOfRangeException. The cumulative probabilities the search bisects over are dumped beside the answers, so a port that disagrees on the CDF can be told apart from one whose search is wrong.

Each answer is printed beside the cumulative probabilities the search bisects over and the mean and variance that decide whether the Chebyshev narrowing runs at all, so a port that disagrees on the CDF can be told apart from one whose search is wrong. suites.title: VariantContextComparator: contig order, then start
suites.why: H.2, and one of the two things gatk-rs's MultiVariantDataSource needs: the multi-input walkers gatk-rs G1.6 handed over cannot be ported until this and VCFUtils.smartMergeHeaders exist. Three behaviours are the reason for the case list. The two constructors refuse different things and word them differently: from a contig list the index is the position so only a repeated name can go wrong, while from header lines the index is carried by the line, so a repeated INDEX is a second, separately-worded error that a contig list cannot express at all — and the empty case is refused by both with different sentences, which the port got wrong until this dump said so. An unknown contig throws NullPointerException, and htsjdk's own comment says it does so happily, meaning a caller sorting a variant outside the dictionary gets an exception rather than an arbitrary order. And compare returns a subtraction rather than a normalised sign, so the magnitude is observable and the dump records the number: a comparator built from lines with sparse indexes returns the difference of those indexes, not of their positions in the collection.

suites.title: VCFUtils.smartMergeHeaders: what survives, and in what order
suites.why: H.2, and the second of the two things gatk-rs's MultiVariantDataSource needs: with this and VariantContextComparator the multi-input walkers gatk-rs G1.6 handed over become portable. Eighty lines of Java, and most of what matters in them is not the merge, which is why the suite exists. THE OUTPUT ALWAYS CARRIES A fileformat LINE NO SOURCE WROTE: getMetaDataInSortedOrder prepends one before the sorted metadata, so a merge of two headers holding one INFO line each returns two lines rather than one, and the extra one is VCFv4.2 unless the header's version FIELD is 4.3 or later — a field set at parse time, not a fileformat line among the metadata, so a header assembled in memory never reaches the version policy however its lines are labelled. THE TWO PROMOTION ARMS ARE BOTH NO-OPS: the Java says promote key to Float in each and neither does it, because the put writes back what the map already holds, so an Integer seen first stays Integer and a Float seen first stays Float. The one branch that does change the map is setNumberToUnbounded, which mutates the stored line in place. And the input order is each source's SORTED order, not its file order, which is what the method's own comment says the ordering exists to protect for contig lines.

suites.title: The .idx file, and the blocks a query resolves to
suites.why: H.2's last named consumer, and the item gatk-rs G1.3 named when it closed: the Tribble index is what turns a Feature file into a random-access source rather than a linear read. The dump was written before the port on purpose, and it earned that order three times over. The index type identifiers cannot be read reliably out of the source at all, because LinearIndex.INDEX_TYPE reads a field of the IndexType enum whose own constructor is handed LinearIndex.INDEX_TYPE; measured here, they are 1 for linear and 2 for interval tree, under the magic number 1480870228, which is TIDX. The bin width is PER CONTIG rather than a constant — 16000 for one contig and 8000 for another in the same file — so a port that took a constant would be wrong without ever failing. And the raw bytes are NOT STABLE ACROSS RUNS: the header carries indexedFileTS, the source file's modification time, so a golden built on them would fail intermittently or, worse, be repaired by regenerating it. That was measured by running the dump twice and diffing rather than reasoned about, and the eight bytes are zeroed with their offset reported so the rest of the layout stays under test. The query rows pin three things the port would otherwise guess: the longest feature is subtracted from the start so a query reaches features that begin before the interval, the answer is always one merged block or none because linear blocks are adjacent by definition, and an unknown contig THROWS rather than returning an empty list.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner. 29 rows, and now BOTH index layouts: the linear one, whose N blocks are rebuilt from N+1 positions with the sizes derived, and the interval-tree one, whose sizes are stored and whose coordinates are 1-based where the BED was 0-based. Reading either with the other's assumptions produces plausible nonsense rather than an error, which is why the two are compared separately. The .idx bytes carry a masked timestamp because indexedFileTS was measured to change on every run.

suites.title: Building a .idx, and the decisions that shape it
suites.why: The read side of the Tribble index landed in htsjdk-rs #83; this is the write side, which GATK runs beside every VCF it emits. Reading is a layout and writing is a set of decisions the layout only records the outcome of, and four of those decisions are invisible in the file. THE BIN WIDTH IS NOT THE ONE THE CREATOR WAS GIVEN: LinearIndex.optimize doubles it PER CONTIG, merging blocks pairwise, until the most dense block is estimated to hold more than MAX_FEATURES_PER_BIN features, or one block is left, or the width goes bad. That is the cause of the outcome the read suite measured, 16000 for one contig and 8000 for another in one file, and the loop keeps the LAST width still under the threshold rather than the first one over it. THE DENSITY IS ESTIMATED, NEVER COUNTED: the score is the largest block's size in BYTES over the mean bytes per feature, never compared to the feature count the same object carries, so two files with the same feature counts and different line lengths optimize differently. THE DYNAMIC CREATOR PICKS THE TYPE FROM THE DATA, and measured here the choice flips BOTH WAYS on the same two files: sparse data gets a linear index under FOR_SEEK_TIME and an interval tree under FOR_SIZE, and dense data gets the opposite, with nothing on a command line to say which a run produced. AND THE STATISTICS IN THE HEADER ARE NOT THE FEATURE LENGTHS: stats.push(longestFeatureLength) pushes the running MAXIMUM, so on features of lengths 10, 10, 600, 10, 10 the FEATURE_LENGTH_MEAN written into the bytes is 364.0, the mean of 10, 10, 600, 600, 600. A port computing the honest mean writes a different file. Both layouts are written, and the interval-tree one is the harder half: its per-contig record is tree.getIntervals(), a PRE-ORDER walk of a red-black tree rather than a sorted list, so the byte order is the order the rotations left the nodes in and the insert comparator sending EQUAL STARTS LEFT is part of the file. Two refusals are measured with their messages, and one of them states the OPPOSITE of the condition it guards: an empty file throws 'finalFilePosition != 0, -> 0' from a check that fires when it IS zero.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the candidate-goldens artefact of the golden-pending run of htsjdk-rs #99. 33 rows: 10 built indexes, 10 property sets, 10 per-contig records and 3 refusals. ALL THIRTEEN cases are compared, ten of them BYTE FOR BYTE across both layouts and three by the refusal they produce, with the header's path, size, timestamp and MD5 taken from the golden because they are facts about the run rather than decisions of the creator; everything else, the properties and every contig record, the port produces. suites.title: ITF8 and LTF8, the integers CRAM is measured in
suites.why: The floor of H.3. A container header is a run of ITF8s, a slice header is a run of ITF8s, and a compression header's encoding parameters are ITF8s inside a byte array, so nothing above them can be checked until they are. Two properties are not in the specification. THE FIVE-BYTE ITF8 STORES FOUR BITS TWICE: the writer puts (value >> 4) & 0xFF in byte four and value & 0xFF in byte five, and the reader takes byte four whole while masking byte five to its low nibble, so f000000112 and f0000001f2 both read 18 and a stream whose two copies disagree resolves silently to byte four's. A port that reads the fifth byte whole answers differently on exactly those streams. AND A TRUNCATED STREAM IS A NUMBER, NOT A REFUSAL: InputStream.read() returns -1 at end of stream and nothing checks it after the first byte, so the two-byte form 80 reads -1 and the five-byte form f000 reads -1. Only a stream empty at the FIRST byte throws, and it throws RuntimeEOFException with a null message. So a truncated CRAM does not fail here, it produces a number. Reproducing the refusal a port would naturally add would be the divergence. Negative ints also round-trip through the five-byte form, so "unsigned" in the method name is a misnomer the type does not carry.

suites.title: The bit stream the core codecs are written on
suites.why: The floor under the encodings, the way ITF8 is the floor under the frames: three of the codecs the encoding map names are written on a BIT stream rather than a byte one. BITS GO IN MOST SIGNIFICANT FIRST, left-aligned into a one-byte buffer held back until it fills, so a one-bit 1 is 0x80 rather than 0x01. FLUSH PADS THE PARTIAL BYTE WITH ZEROS ON THE RIGHT and nothing records how many bits were real, so a stream of one true bit and a stream of 0x80 in eight bits are the same byte and only the count of values a reader expects says where the stream ends. A MULTI-BYTE WRITE SPLITS AT THE TOP, writing whole bytes from the most significant end while eight bits remain and the remainder last, so the leftover bits of a twelve-bit write are the LOW four. A VALUE WIDER THAN ITS DECLARED WIDTH IS MASKED, not refused. THE BOUNDS ARE CHECKED WITH THREE DIFFERENT WORDINGS, one per overload, AND ONE CASE IS NOT CHECKED AT ALL: write(byte, 0) against a non-empty buffer indexes a mask table of eight entries with 8, so writing nothing is a no-op or an exception depending on what came before it. AND END OF STREAM IS AN EXCEPTION RATHER THAN A ZERO, with no way to ask the stream how many bits are left.

suites.title: Beta, Gamma and Subexponential, the three codecs on the bit stream
suites.why: The three codecs the encoding map can name that write on the bit stream rather than on an external byte block. The dump drives each through the slice-blocks streams the reader and writer really use and takes the RAW CORE BLOCK back out, so what it records is what would land in a file. EVERY CODEC CARRIES AN OFFSET, added before storage and subtracted after, which is how a range starting below zero is stored in bits that cannot hold a sign. BETA IS THE ONLY ONE OF THE THREE WITH AN UPPER BOUND, refusing what does not fit with two messages naming the value, the offset and the limit. GAMMA AND SUBEXPONENTIAL COMPUTE A BIT LENGTH WITH A FLOATING-POINT LOG, 1 + (int)(Math.log(v) / Math.log(2)), so the bytes written depend on a double division landing on the right side of an integer at every power of two; the corpus walks every one of them up to 2^31 - 1. GAMMA REFUSES ZERO AND BELOW because its length prefix cannot encode a value with no bits. SUBEXPONENTIAL HAS TWO REGIMES SPLIT AT 2^k, and above the split the top bit is implied by the unary prefix rather than written. AND TWO OF THE FOUR MESSAGES CARRY A QUIRK: a double space in Gamma's, and 'less then' in Subexponential's.

suites.title: Canonical Huffman, the fourth codec on the bit stream
suites.why: A CRAM file carries no Huffman tree. It carries an alphabet and one code word length per symbol, and both writer and reader rebuild the same code words from that pair alone, so what the suite pins is THE REBUILDING and not the tree that chose the lengths (htsjdk has a class for that and nothing in the library calls it). Symbols are grouped by length, sorted inside each group, and handed consecutive integers shifted left whenever the length grows, so THE ALPHABET'S ORDER IN THE FILE DOES NOT MATTER. BYTE SYMBOLS SORT SIGNED, the grouping being a TreeSet, so 0x80 takes the first code word and not the last. A ONE-SYMBOL ALPHABET HAS LENGTH ZERO and therefore writes no bits at all, leaving an empty core block from which the number of symbols written cannot be recovered. THE OVERFLOW CHECK COUNTS SET BITS RATHER THAN WIDTH, so three symbols at one bit are accepted and the third given code word 2, while four are refused. AND AN UNMATCHED CODE WORD RUNS OFF THE END OF A TABLE SIZED TO THE LARGEST CODE WORD, so a truncated or foreign stream is an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and the codec's own 'unable to map' message is reachable only with an empty alphabet.

suites.title: The codecs written on external blocks, and the two built out of them
suites.why: Six of the encoding map's identifiers put their data in a block of its own, named by a content id, and two more are built out of the first six. A block is bytes rather than bits, so what these codecs carry instead of alignment is a set of decisions about where one value ends and the next begins. EACH CODEC NAMES A BLOCK AND TWO CODECS CAN NAME THE SAME ONE, which is what lets a ByteArrayLen put its lengths and its bytes in one block, interleaved; the corpus has that arrangement and the separate-block one side by side. EXTERNAL BYTE CANNOT SEE THE END OF ITS BLOCK: it returns (byte) stream.read(), which past the end is -1, and a byte of 0xFF that is really there reads back as -1 too. BYTE ARRAY STOP TRUSTS THE DATA, so an array holding the stop byte is written whole and read back SPLIT with nothing reporting it, and a block that ends before a stop byte does is not an error either. AND BYTE ARRAY LEN CANNOT WRAP BYTE ARRAY STOP FOR READING though the format lets it: the length is read, then the stop codec's read(length) throws 'Not implemented.' Every refusal row carries the block it was read from, so no test can rebuild an input from a label.

suites.title: Golomb, Golomb-Rice and Golomb-Long, the three the specification is removing
suites.why: Experimental in the reference, and reachable all the same: the encoding factory dispatches to them by identifier, so a file that names one has to be read and a port that skips them cannot claim to read every legal file. htsjdk logs a warning when one is built and guards them no further. GOLOMB DOES NOT ROUND-TRIP A VALUE WHOSE OFFSET SUM IS NEGATIVE and does not say so: with offset 0 and m 4, -1 is written as 60 and read back as 3, because the quotient is written by counting up to it and a negative one writes nothing at all. GOLOMB-RICE'S PARAMETER IS NOT m: the encoding calls it m and hands it to the codec as log2m, so an encoding built with 8 divides by 256 and 255 costs a byte and a half where 256 costs two. GOLOMB REFUSES m BELOW 2 AND GOLOMB-RICE TAKES IT WITHOUT A WORD, so the same mistake is an exception in one and a different encoding in the other. THE TWO REFUSALS OF read(length) ARE WORDED DIFFERENTLY, 'Multi-value read method not defined.' against 'Not implemented.' And every value in the corpus is small next to its m, because the quotient is unary: one long of 2^32 with m of 10 writes four hundred million ones, a row measured once at a hundred megabytes and removed.

suites.title: EncodingFactory: which encoding a type and an identifier resolve to
suites.why: The last thing between a file's bytes and the codecs: a compression header names an encoding per data series, by identifier and parameters, and this turns that pair into something that can read. Forty lines of Java, and one missing keyword in them. THE SWITCH FALLS THROUGH: only the BYTE arm ends in a break, so an INT that matches nothing falls into the LONG arm and then into the BYTE_ARRAY arm, and a LONG that matches nothing falls into BYTE_ARRAY. An INT data series named with BYTE_ARRAY_LEN therefore gets a ByteArrayLenEncoding rather than the refusal the method's last line promises, and BYTE never falls through at all. THE PARAMETERS ARE NOT CHECKED AGAINST THE TYPE, so the same bytes mean a content id in one arm and the head of a Huffman alphabet in another. NULL IS AN IDENTIFIER LIKE ANY OTHER and matches nothing anywhere, so all four types refuse it, with a message naming both halves of what was asked for. The suite is exhaustive by construction: four types by ten identifiers, every cell recorded as the class it produced or the refusal it raised.

suites.title: The compression header as a whole, and the checksum version 3 carries
suites.why: Three length-prefixed maps inside one raw block, each already covered by a suite of its own. This is the join, and the last structure between a container's bytes and the codecs that read its slices. A HEADER READ AND WRITTEN AGAIN IS BYTE-IDENTICAL in all six measured cases, which is the property a byte-identical port needs and the one place a dropped field shows without being looked for. THE VERSION CHANGES THE BLOCK AND NOTHING INSIDE IT: a 3.0 block carries a four-byte CRC-32 that a 2.1 block does not, so the same header is 178 bytes in one and 174 in the other, identical up to those four. The checksum covers the block header and the content together, is written little-endian, and sits OUTSIDE the compressed size. THE BLOCK IS ALWAYS RAW whatever the version, and its content type is checked before anything is parsed, with the refusal naming what was found. TWO OF THE FIVE PRESERVATION KEYS ARE REQUIRED and one message covers a missing SM and a missing TD alike, fired only after the whole map has been read; an unknown key is fatal and carries the two characters that were not recognised.

suites.title: The slice header, and the six tags that ride in it
suites.why: The last frame before CRAM becomes reads. THE BLOCK COUNT DOES NOT COUNT THE HEADER BLOCK: getNumberOfBlocks returns 1 + numberOfExternalBlocks, and measured on five files it equals exactly the number of blocks that FOLLOW the header, so a reader that counts the header among them stops one short. SIX TAGS RIDE IN THE HEADER AND FOUR OF THEM DIGEST NOTHING: B1 and S1 carry a SHA-1, B5 and S5 a SHA-512, and on an unmapped slice all four are the digest of the EMPTY string, byte for byte identical in every file, which is 168 bytes of constant per slice. Only BD and SD move with the reads, and they do NOT move when only the record tags change, which two files differing in exactly that prove. THE TAG SECTION HAS NO LENGTH: it is read to the end of the block, so the block's own length is the only delimiter and a header with no tags is indistinguishable from one whose tags are zero bytes long. THE MD5 IS SIXTEEN ZEROES WHEN THERE IS NONE, so its emptiness is a value rather than an absence. AN ABSENT EMBEDDED REFERENCE IS -1 written as an ITF8, which is the FIVE-byte form, so the commonest value of the field is also its longest encoding. AND THE TAG SECTION IS VERSION-GATED ON BOTH SIDES, so the same slice is shorter in a 2.1 file.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the candidate-goldens-golden-pending-11 artefact of run 31049831397, the golden-pending run of htsjdk-rs #122. 51 rows over five files: 5 slice headers whole in hex and 5 more field by field, 5 declared block counts beside the blocks that actually follow, 30 decoded slice tags, 5 slice counts and the constants. The tags are decoded with the reader's own codec rather than read off the bytes, which is what showed there are six of them and not one. Two of the five files differ only in whether their records carry tags, which is what separates the digests that move from the digests that do not.

suites.title: How a record becomes read features, and what a match costs
suites.why: The first half of the CRAM record model. A slice's records are not stored as bases and a cigar: they are an alignment start, a read length, and a list of read features, and EVERYTHING THAT MATCHES THE REFERENCE IS STORED AS NOTHING AT ALL. THE POSITIONS ARE ONE-BASED AND THE INTERFACE SAYS THEY ARE NOT: every construction site passes zeroBasedPositionInRead + 1 while ReadFeature.getPosition's javadoc says zero-based, so a port that believes the doc is off by one on every feature. AN INSERTION OF n BASES BECOMES n FEATURES AND A SOFT CLIP OF n BECOMES ONE, decided five lines apart in the same loop, and htsjdk's own comment says the insertion should use a Bases feature and does not, so Bases and Insertion are read and never written. A MISMATCH SPLITS ON THE ALPHABET, NOT ON THE CIGAR: an ACGTN-to-ACGTN mismatch is a Substitution and anything else is a ReadBase carrying the quality score a second time. THE CIGAR'S OWN CLAIM IS NOT CONSULTED: an X over bases that match emits nothing and an = over bases that differ emits substitutions. PAST THE END OF THE REFERENCE EVERY BASE IS COMPARED AGAINST N, so an N out there matches and four Ns at the end of the reference produce three features. SEQ=* MANUFACTURES Ns that then mismatch, one substitution per position. AND THE MISSING-QUALITY TEST IS AN IDENTITY TEST: baseQualities.equals(NULL_QUALS) is Object.equals on a byte[], so an equal but distinct empty array is indexed like any other and throws.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the candidate-goldens-cram-read-features artefact of run 31096812285, the golden-pending run of htsjdk-rs #124. 124 rows over twenty cases and one reference that is deliberately not all ACGT, so a base outside ACGTN can be met on the reference side as well as the read side. The twelve operator letters come from the classes rather than from the specification. Two cases end in an exception and carry their inputs like every other row.

suites.title: The cigar rebuilt from read features, where the matches are the gaps
suites.why: The way back from the read features. THE CIGAR IS NOT STORED ANYWHERE: it is rebuilt from the feature positions and the read length, and `gap = position - (lastOpPos + lastOpLen)` is the ONLY source of M in the output, so the matches thrown away on the way in come back as the gaps between what was kept. A SUBSTITUTION AND A READBASE ARE BOTH M, so the rebuilt cigar never emits X or =, and a record written with 8X comes back as 8M: the only shape in the corpus whose round trip changes. A FEATURE THAT CONSUMES NO READ BASES WINDS THE READ CURSOR BACK, because the bookkeeping is in read space, and a deletion at the first position therefore leaves the whole read after it: D@1 len=2 over a read of 8 rebuilds as 2D8M. THE SWITCH SILENTLY IGNORES WHAT IT DOES NOT NAME, dropping BaseQualityScore, Scores and Bases, and Bases carries read bases, so a list holding one rebuilds as though it were not there. AND THE READ LENGTH SAYS WHERE THE READ ENDS AND IT WINS: a feature positioned past it is absorbed, and a read length of 0 takes the accumulated length instead.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the candidate-goldens-cram-record-cigar artefact of run 31110570337, the golden-pending run of htsjdk-rs #126. 40 rows: twenty-six hand-built feature lists, so the rebuild is exercised on shapes the writer never emits as well as on shapes it does, and thirteen round trips of a record's own cigar through its features and back. Every row carries the list it came from.

suites.title: The bases restored, in two passes and through a signed lookup
suites.why: The last piece of the record model's reverse direction. The bases come from three sources at once: the features say what differs, the reference supplies everything else, and the substitution matrix turns a code back into a base. IT IS TWO PASSES AND THE SECOND ONE OVERWRITES: ReadBase and Bases are skipped in the main loop under a comment saying to defer them, then applied straight into the array, so they win over the reference fill and over what the features before them wrote, and an insertion of GGG at position 1 followed by a Bases of TTT at position 1 restores TTT. THE TRAILING FILL STOPS AT THE END OF THE REFERENCE and leaves the array's own zeros: nothing ever writes an N past the end, a zero becomes one on the way through the lookup. toBamReadBasesInPlace INDEXES A 127-BYTE TABLE WITH A SIGNED BYTE, so a base of 0xE9 is index -23 and a base of 127 is one past the end, and because the table is built by adding 32 to every BAM read base, ']' is an '=' rather than an N. A SUBSTITUTION RESOLVES AGAINST A NORMALIZED REFERENCE BASE, so an IUPAC code on the reference resolves as though it were N. AND UNKNOWN BASES OR A READ LENGTH OF ZERO RETURN THE EMPTY SEQUENCE, with the features not looked at at all. The reference used here is aperiodic on purpose: against ACGTACGT... a reference cursor off by four reads the same bases as a correct one.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the candidate-goldens-cram-restore-bases artefact of run 31112240771, the golden-pending run of htsjdk-rs #128. 55 rows: twenty-four cases, six failures with the reference's own exception and message, eighteen entries of the lookup table every restored base goes through, and the five rows of the substitution matrix the cases are resolved against. The reference is aperiodic on purpose: against ACGTACGT... a cursor off by four reads the same bases as a correct one, and every case would pass anyway.

suites.title: commons-math3's MersenneTwister and the permutation a fingerprint metric draws from it
suites.why: commons-math3 seeds from an int with Knuth's multiplier and skips the array-seeding step the reference algorithm runs, so its stream is not a textbook MT19937's. Each accessor consumes its own words, which makes the ORDER of calls part of the answer, and nextPermutation is a partial Fisher-Yates whose first k entries are the result.

cases.why: Five seeds including zero and both extremes, twelve draws of each accessor, four bounds including a power of two, a mixed sequence that shows each accessor consuming its own words, five permutations including a partial one and one of a single element, the index-map direction a caller reads a permutation in, and the three bound pairs whose refusals name what they were given.

probes.title: Decision 0019: is re-sorting a sorted VCF header still a no-op?
probes.on_failure: Re-sorting is no longer stable. Decision 0019 needs revisiting.
probes.why: The port relies on it: writing a header that has already been through the comparator once must not reorder it. Measured stable, not proven stable, so it is re-measured.

probes.title: Decision 0016: is the VCF header comparator still inconsistent?
probes.on_failure: The comparator is now consistent. Decision 0016 can be revisited.
probes.why: The cycle is the reason the port uses a total order where htsjdk has none. If a future htsjdk made the comparator consistent, this fails and the divergence can be removed.

goldens_handled_elsewhere.why: Compared function by function against a corpus regenerated on real silicon, with per-function pass conditions from decision 0007, rather than by byte equality.
